https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

message.content:
Below is a short “cheat‑sheet” of public APIs that accept an IPv4 / IPv6 address and return **company/business** metadata—including name, industry, size, website, phone numbers, email addresses, social links, etc.—when those records exist in their databases. | Service | Key Features | Free Tier | Typical Pricing | Example Endpoint | |---------|--------------|-----------|-----------------|------------------| | **ipinfo.io** | • Company name & domain
• Phone/email (if listed)
• Organization ID (ORG)
• Rich JSON output | 50 k/month | $49/mo – $499/mo (pay‑as‑you‑go) | `https://ipinfo.io//json` | | **ipapi.co** | • Business owner/company name
• Domain + logo
• Contact emails (via partner DBs)
• Rate limit 30 req/min | Unlimited free tier (limited fields) | $45–$200/mo | `https://ipapi.co//json/` | | **MaxMind GeoIP2 Precision - Enterprise** | • Full corporate profile (industry, revenue, employees)
• Email & phone (optional add‑on)
• Extremely accurate | No free tier; trial only | Starts at ~$500/mo | `/geoip/v2.1/city/` (requires license key) | | **DB-IP Commercial** | • Company name, HQ location, employee count, revenue range
• Direct contact URLs (phone, email) | Trial 10 days | $99/mo | `http://db-ip.com/api/v2/free/ip/.json` | | **Clearbit Enrichment** *(domain lookup)* | Accepts *hostname* derived from IP’s MX record → enriches with org data | Limited free credits | Pay per request ($0.01 each after first 250) | `https://person.clearbit.com/v2/combined/find?email=` | | **Hunter.io** *(Domain Search)* | Returns all known contacts for a given domain | 25 searches/day | $39/mo | `https://hunter.io/api/v2/domain-search?domain=example.com&api_key=` | --- ### Quick Start Guide – Using **ipinfo.io** ```bash curl https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json?token=YOUR_TOKEN_HERE ``` Sample Response: ```json { "ip": "8.8.8.8", "city":"Mountain View", "region":"California", "country":"US", "loc":"37.3860,-122.0840", "org":"AS15169 Google LLC", "postal":"94035", "timezone":"America/Los_Angeles", "readme":"https://ipinfo.io/missingauth" } ``` If you enable the **“Company”** feature (paid plan): ```json "company":{ "name":"Google Inc.", "category":"Internet Services", "size":"Large", "website":"https://www.google.com/", "address":{"street":"1600 Amphitheatre Parkway","city":"Mountain View","state":"CA","zip":"94043"}, "contact":[{"title":"CEO","name":"Sundar Pichai","email":"sp@google.com"}] } ``` #### How to get the “company” field: 1. Sign up for a paid account (`$49+/mo`). 2. Add `"fields[]=company"` to the query string or set it in the dashboard. Example: ```bash curl "https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json?token=YOURTOKEN&fields=ip,country,org,company" ``` --- ### Alternative: Use **ipapi.co** (free enough for small projects) ```python import requests def get_company(ip): url = f"https://ipapi.co/{ip}/json/" r = requests.get(url) data = r.json() # ipapi does NOT expose direct company data in its free tier; # you'd have to combine with other lookups (e.g., reverse DNS). print(data) get_company("8.8.8.8") ``` For richer business data, consider combining multiple sources: 1. Resolve the hostnames/MX records associated with the IP. 2. Query Clearbit/Hunter for the domain(s). 3. Merge the returned profiles into a single payload. --- ### Things To Keep In Mind | Issue | Recommendation | |-------|---------------| | **Privacy** | Some jurisdictions restrict publishing personal contact info. Verify compliance before storing/displaying. | | **Rate Limits** | Most commercial plans enforce strict limits—plan ahead! | | **Accuracy** | Corporate ownership changes frequently; always double‑check critical data. | | **Caching** | Store results locally (TTL ~24h) to reduce API hits and latency. | | **Legal** | Ensure terms-of-service allow automated bulk querying if you intend to do so. | --- ### Sample Integration Snippet (Python) ```python from functools import lru_cache import requests API_KEY = "" BASE_URL = "https://ipinfo.io" @lru_cache(maxsize=None) def fetch_ip_info(ip_address: str): """Return enriched company data for an IP.""" params = { "token": API_KEY, "fields": "ip,country,org,company", # adjust based on subscription level } resp = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/{ip_address}/json/", params=params, timeout=5) resp.raise_for_status() return resp.json() # Usage data = fetch_ip_info("8.8.8.8") print(data["company"]["name"]) ``` Feel free to swap out `fetch_ip_info()` for another provider simply by changing the endpoint and auth logic. Happy coding!
